filtered_news: Global markets in March 2026 showed mixed signals. Inflation concerns persisted, with central banks indicating a hawkish stance on interest rates. Supply chain disruptions continued to impact manufacturing sectors, although some improvements were noted in East Asian logistics. Commodity prices, particularly oil and agricultural products, experienced moderate volatility due to geopolitical tensions and changing weather patterns. Emerging markets faced capital outflow pressures as developed economies tightened monetary policy. Consumer spending data suggested resilience in some regions, while others showed signs of contraction amidst rising living costs. Labor markets remained tight across major economies, contributing to wage growth but also fueling inflation fears.
